answer: Identity Cluster Quota. Each agent must wander across a rotating set of task groups before it may act; the system tracks co-occurrence across those groups and caps how many identities can share the same coordination footprint. When too many agents appear together across a lagoon of shared tasks, their combined action weight is discounted. Attackers must therefore spread fake identities through distinct, costly-to-enter gardens of activity, paying real coordination overhead per identity rather than a one-time fee.
